title: Borrowing without drowning in repayments
target: How to take a loan in Supermarket Simulator and live with it, given that the game sets a term length, a daily payment and a daily interest, and keeps a bankruptcy path if it goes wrong.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is already trading
A reason for the money that pays for itself
An idea of what a day currently earns

steps.do: Decide what the money is for before opening the loan screen.
steps.because: the loan screen ships its own amount and daily-interest labels rather than a single figure (Loan Amount Text, Daily Interest)

steps.do: Set the term length deliberately rather than accepting the first value.
steps.because: a loan has a term length of its own, with a slider and a text field for it (Loan Term Length Slider, Loan Term Length Text)

steps.do: Read the daily payment as a cost per day, not as a total.
steps.because: the screen names a daily payment object of its own, with a label beside it (Daily Payment, Daily Payment Text)

steps.do: Check the repayment tab before the end of the day rather than after it.
steps.because: repayments have their own interface tab (RepaymentTab)

steps.do: Know where the bankruptcy path is before you need it.
steps.because: the game has a bankruptcy path and its own screen for it (BankruptcyScreen)

commonMistakes: Borrowing for stock that will not sell before the payments land.
Taking the longest term without checking what the daily interest does to a day's profit.
Waiting for the repayment tab to warn you instead of reading it yourself.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
